quickIntro: I graduated from Soochow University in Taiwan in June 2025, majoring in Japanese, and moved to Japan at the end of August 2025. Since October 2025, I've been working as a full-time Frontend Engineer at Reazon Holdings, building and maintaining the menu app (native and web) with React Native and Next.js. With my Japanese/English/Mandarin proficiency and frontend skills, I aim to make meaningful contributions to both users and the team.
workAchievement1: Owned end-to-end frontend implementation for major campaigns — "Same In-Store Pricing" and "New Store Review Rewards" — spanning the full user flow from TOP-page entry points through store and cart screens to post-purchase confirmation, including A/B-tested UI and flow variants.
workAchievement2: Paid down technical debt alongside feature work — breaking apart oversized, prop-heavy components with tangled conditionals, and fixing a bug where duplicate side-effect hook calls were triggering redundant API requests.
workAchievement3: Helped migrate the entire app from react-navigation to expo-router as part of the team.
workAchievement4: Used Sentry for error and performance monitoring, and partnered with the business team to design Firebase Analytics event tracking for new campaigns — defining which actions fire which events and which screens drive purchases — to support campaign and conversion analysis.
workAchievement5: Used the company's AI-driven, spec-first development workflow (internally called "AX") — spec/Figma/codebase → AI-generated requirements → design doc → implementation — to ship real features, and shared feedback based on hands-on use.
internAchievement2: Collaborated with the PO on prototyping: built lightweight prototypes to align on the PO's vision before specs were finalized, then quickly polished styles once design comps were ready, keeping development moving smoothly.
internAchievement3: Clarified ambiguous specs: while implementing against design comps, surfaced gaps between the PO's intent and the actual designs and raised them in meetings to drive team discussion.
internAchievement4: Built a data-visualization dashboard with Recharts: preprocessed raw API data on the frontend to show enterprise clients regional revenue trends as a line chart and charging-station utilization as a 100% stacked area chart, helping them quickly judge where to open new locations.
skillsSubtitle: Tools and technologies I work with.
whyFrontendDescription: Most of my Japanese-major peers go into the service industry after graduation, but a part-time customer-service job taught me I wanted work built around depth and problem-solving, not one-off interactions. I still enjoy working as part of a team, so that stayed important to me — and it's what led me to start learning programming, something I'd always been curious about, and eventually find my footing in frontend development.
howFrontendTitle1: 2024 Feb-Mar. My First Step into Coding
howFrontendDetails1: Started from zero with HTML/CSS/JavaScript on freeCodeCamp — hands-on challenges that got me hooked on solving problems with code.
howFrontendTitle2: 2024 Apr-Jun. Realizing My Passion on Frontend Development
howFrontendDetails2: Went deeper with an advanced JavaScript course on Udemy, which built real confidence writing code on my own — and confirmed I wanted to build things people can actually see and interact with.
howFrontendDetails3: Learned React through a project-based React course, building everything from small tools to more complete apps.
howFrontendTitle4: 2024 Sep-2025 Jun. From Learning to Doing
howFrontendDetails4: Built a portfolio project with Vanilla JS, used it to land a frontend internship, and started shipping production React + TypeScript code with a real team — turning everything I'd learned into something real.
sideProjectsSubtitle: A couple of things I've built while learning.
nihongoDescription: Built before I'd touched any frontend framework — pure JavaScript, HTML and CSS, with all state and view updates handled by hand and data persisted to localStorage.
nihongoDetails: A vocabulary tool for Japanese learners: build a custom word list, then get quizzed with randomized fill-in-the-blank questions (word / reading / meaning) and a scored review of what you missed.
handDripperDescription: A full-stack pour-over coffee app built with React, TypeScript and Vite — Supabase handles auth and the Postgres database, TanStack Query handles data fetching and caching.
handDripperDetails: Lets home baristas log brewing variables (ratio, water temperature, grind size, technique) and auto-calculates water amount from the coffee-to-water ratio. Smart input suggestions surface each user's 4 most recent beans/drippers/shops/grinders to speed up entry, a built-in timer tracks brew time, and a searchable history lets users sort, filter, pin and edit past recipes.
